title: tenant surge cost sculptor + graceful quantization failsafe
author: Nina K. Park
description:
Motivation: Large tenants occasionally generate short-lived traffic surges that cause suboptimal batching and KV cache thrashing; naive fallbacks to lower-priced variants sometimes cause unacceptable quality regressions. This PR introduces a tenant-aware Cost Sculptor component that synthesizes per-tenant cost/latency curves from live telemetry and automatically applies a conservative quantization fallback when spike-safe thresholds are met. The goal is to reduce unit token cost during bursts while keeping degradation bounded and observable.

What this implements: 
- A lightweight cost model builder (pkg/costsculptor) that consumes sampled latency, token, and model-variant telemetry to produce a compact cost curve per tenant. The builder supports exponential decay windows and configurable lookback.
- An admission controller hook in the serving runtime that consults tenant curves and applies an orchestration decision: (1) prefer microbatch routing within the same model family, (2) apply a conservative int8-ish quant profile when allowed, and (3) enable a short-lived KV-prefill mode to warm caches for predicted hot shards.
- Conservative quantization profiles and a failsafe: quant fallbacks are tagged and routed through a degraded-quality guard that enforces token limits and side-by-side eval capture for rollback. The default profile is intentionally conservative (minimal weight clipping, awareness of softmax temperature sensitivity).
- A small CLI (cli/costctl) to preview a tenant's cost curve, simulate a surge, and generate a canary rollout plan (10% -> 50% -> 100%) plus suggested telemetry thresholds.
- Helm values and an operator patch to expose tenant policies (helm/redwood/values.yaml updates).
- E2E smoke tests and a replay harness for unit-econ simulation under synthetic surges (test/e2e/cost-sculptor-replay).

Checklist: 
- [x] cost model builder + tests
- [x] runtime admission hook and gating logic
- [x] conservative quant profiles + telemetry tagging
- [x] CLI and helm integration
- [x] e2e replay and CI smoke tests
- [x] docs (docs/cost-sculptor.md) with rollout guidance and safety notes

Rollout plan: Start as opt-in via tenant policy flags. Default deployment will add the admission hook disabled; chart values enable gradual activation. Canary route configured at 10% traffic with automatic rollback on quality-regression signals.

Related: ENG-4122 (tenant surge detection), ENG-4210 (quantization safety gates), SUP-1223 (customer incident that motivated conservative fallback).
commits: feat(costsculptor): add cost curve synthesizer and decay window algorithms
feat(runtime): add tenant admission hook for surge-aware routing and quant hinting
chore(helm): expose tenant policy toggles in values.yaml
test(e2e): add replay harness and smoke tests for surge scenarios
docs: add operational runbook and rollout guidance for Cost Sculptor
review_comments: Ethan Morales: Please add a metric tag so we can filter post-hoc by tenant and rollout id; also prefer a less-aggressive default decay window (30s -> 5m) to avoid flip-flop during noisy traffic.
Nina K. Park: Addressed — added rollout_id tags and changed default decay to 2m with configuration in helm values. Expanded docs with examples for window tuning.

Priya Nair: The quant fallback looks reasonable but we need a safety net for hallucination regressions — can we ensure side-by-side evals capture the first 100 outputs and fail fast on a regression signal?

Nina K. Park: Added a degraded-quality guard that captures side-by-side outputs for the first 500 tokens per tenant per deployment and wires a regression alert metric. We keep the default conservative enough that this should be rare; captured traces are sent to the eval pipeline for automatic diffing.
Liam Chen: CI flake on linux/arm transiently failed in first run — re-ran and green. Approving the approach and configuration defaults.
Ethan Morales: Approval after telemetry tag and decay tuning changes. Ship it.
release_notes: Introduce 'Cost Sculptor' tenant-aware surge controller: synthesizes per-tenant cost curves, adds conservative quantization fallback with safety guards, includes CLI and helm toggles, opt-in canary rollout recommended.
